title: What Is a PSA 10? Gem Mint Grading, Value & PSA 9 Comparison
summary: What does a PSA 10 actually mean? Learn PSA Gem Mint grading criteria, the real price gap between PSA 10 vs PSA 9, and when grading cards is worth the cost.
body_markdown:
[Back in 1976](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/nadia-comaneci-a-pioneer-in-perfection) , an Olympic gymnast approached the uneven bars. Moments later, the scoreboard in Montreal flashed 1.00. No, this wasn’t another[epic Olympic fail](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qu1rA3ZolrI) . Instead, it was the moment Nadia Comăneci changed gymnastics—and cards—forever.


You see, until Comăneci’s performance, no one had ever scored a perfect 10; scoring had topped out at 9.99, so scoreboards weren’t programmed to have a fourth number. Since then, scoring a perfect 10 has become a worldwide symbol of success.


Few hobbies understand the value of a perfect 10 better than the world of trading cards.


[Professional Sports Authenticator](https://www.psacard.com/gradingstandards) , better known as PSA, has[authenticated and graded](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/is-courtyard-io-legit-heres-what-you-need-to-know) over 80 million collectibles since launching in July of 1991. They operate on a 10-point scale, with a PSA 10 serving as the top grade. A PSA 10 Gem Mint is the highest possible condition grade awarded by PSA. It signifies a virtually flawless card with four sharp corners, full original gloss, pristine focus, zero staining, and centering within 55/45 on the front and 75/25 on the back.


However, the premium assigned to PSA 10s over PSA 9s isn’t always worth chasing.


Using[Courtyard’s Price Guide,](https://courtyard.io/prices) we dug into the data to determine the difference between PSA grades, how collectors can buy—and pull—them, and some of the heavy-hitting PSA 10s on our platform.


## **What Is a PSA 10? Why Collectors Grade Cards (and When It Pays)**


PSA describes a Gem Mint 10 as[a virtually perfect card](https://www.psacard.com/gradingstandards) . It has four sharp corners, sharp focus and full original gloss, with no staining of any kind. The image has to be centered within about 55/45 on the front and 75/25 on the back. Needless to say, scoring a perfect 10 isn’t easy.


A PSA 9 (Mint) looks like a 10—until closer inspection turns up a small flaw or two, such as a minor printing imperfection or slightly off-white borders. The gap between the two grades can be as minor as one teeny blemish, but the price gap between the two is often massive.


## **What Is a PSA 10? (PSA Gem Mint Defined)**


- **A third party inspection:** The eye test is one thing, but PSA’s trained graders put each card to the test. Once a card receives a PSA grade, collectors know its exact condition, taking the guesswork out of judging the quality of the card from a photo.
- **Authenticity:** As part of their grading process, PSA authenticates the card, verifying it as genuine so you know that what you see is what you get—and not a scam.
- **Protection:** PSA-graded cards are returned to collectors in a sealed case so they can rest assured it won’t have its corners dinged or receive any wear and tear.
- **Easier sales:** A graded card has a stamp of approval buyers both recognize and appreciate, making negotiating easier.
- **High grades impact prices:** Higher-graded cards are generally easy to sell, as collectors want the highest quality cards available.


## **When Does Grading Actually Pay? (The Math)**


Using[Courtyard’s Price Guide](https://courtyard.io/prices) , anyone can search real-time card values in order to make informed buying and selling decisions. We put it to the test by reviewing sales prices for high-end cards on Courtyard in both a PSA 10 and PSA 9.


The results show that more PSA 9s sell than PSA 10s due to the fewer number of perfect cards, but PSA 10s sell for multiples more than their lesser-graded counterparts, and, in some cases, hundreds of thousands of dollars more. When either buying or selling graded cards, it’s important to check the dollar gap between PSA grades as well as how often each grade sells to get a sense of their value.


However, it’s important to note that not every collector feels the need to receive a PSA 10, as many are happy with PSA 9s and PSA 8s. Sometimes it's the card inside the slab that matters more than the number on the outside.

## **Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ):**


### **What is a PSA 10?**


The top grade from grader and authenticator[Professional Sports Authenticator](https://www.psacard.com/gradingstandards) , better known as PSA. They use a 10-point scale, with a PSA 10, known as a Gem Mint, serving as the best possible score. It means the card has four sharp corners, sharp focus, full gloss, no staining and centering of about 55/45 or better on the front. In short, it’s a perfect card.


### **Are trading cards worth grading?**


It depends. Some prefer graded cards for authenticity, ensuring that what they get is what they paid for. Others are OK with raw cards.


It also depends on the quality of the card. First, check the card's PSA 10 and PSA 9 values using[Courtyard’s Price Guide](https://courtyard.io/prices) .


### **How much more is a PSA 10 worth than a PSA 9?**


The premium depends on the card, but it can be many multiples, and many hundreds of thousands of dollars.


### **Where can I check what a graded card is worth?**


Search the[Courtyard Price Guide](https://courtyard.io/prices) for values by grade.
